text:
Toronto's season has hit its first real crisis week. Three straight losses, outscored 11-4, and the chances say it's earned: 43% of the expected goals across those games. The Leafs are 8-9-2 with 18 points, and our simulations put their playoff chance at 10%, projecting about 82 points. "HONEYMOON'S OVER: Are the Leafs COOKED?" is how The Leafs Nation framed it Sunday night.

The details explain the mood. Toronto takes 47% of the expected goals for the season and has scored about six more goals than its chances usually produce, so the scoreboard has been flattering it, not robbing it. Sergei Bobrovsky is at .862 over his last five starts. Kirill Marchenko is hurt, and his line with Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic had been the team's best by the chances (69%). The top pair of Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh has been outscored 10-6.

There are real positives. Matthews has headlines this week about career-best playmaking and improved health, and his line with Roslovic and Easton Cowan has outscored teams 7-2. Gavin McKenna is in the middle of the noise, from a costly turnover to what Jim Hiller told him at intermission against Montreal. The question is whether this team can defend well enough to make Matthews' good year matter. What to watch: Bobrovsky's next few starts and whether Hiller finds a pair he trusts against top lines.
